Guidance & outlook: We continue to Increase revenue from diverse markets, particularly the Indian aftermarket and exports - which are Core pillars of Lakshya RISE 5000, with a target of generating 40% of revenue from new markets by FY 2029-30.

We are pleased to recommend a final dividend of H1.50 per equity share, taking the total dividend for FY 2025-26 to H2.50 per share, representing a payout of approximately 43.3% of PAT and progressing towards our Lakshya RISE 5000 target of a 50% dividend payout.
The share of Allied (non-spring) products in Aftermarket India expanded 8% in FY 2025-26, up from 6% in FY 2024-25 and 3% in FY 2023-24 - doubling each year.
Growth & demand: Our Aftermarket India revenue grew by approximately 14% in FY 2025-26, marking our highest-ever aftermarket performance for the second consecutive year and the share of allied (non-spring) products in the portfolio expanded to approximately 8%, from 6% in the previous year.
In exports, revenue grew to H53 crore from 17 countries, with the product range broadened to include parabolic springs and allied products alongside leaf springs.
In the CV segment, parabolic springs now represent approximately 30% of total spring demand - and JAI holds a dominant approximately 85% market share in this category.
Margins & costs: Our consolidated EBITDA margin improved significantly to 15.1% from 13.5% in FY 2024-25, the profit after tax margin to 8.8% from 7.9%, and Return on Capital Employed stood at 36% net of bill discounting, against 29% a year earlier reflecting a broad-based recovery in the commercial vehicle industry, operating leverage and disciplined cost execution.
